newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan March M2 money supply up 9.90 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan March M2 money supply up 9.90 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew 9.90 percent in March from a year earlier, the central bank said on Thursday.

March was the third straight month in which the central bank used a revised definition of M2 measure. Analysts have said the new broader definition could be expected to add 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to the figure.
The year-on-year March M2 increase was slightly lower than an average forecast of 10.03 percent compiled from an April 21 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.
The central bank, which announced the figure in a surprised move, did not give a reason for the rise.
The bank had been scheduled to announce the March money supply data on Friday at noon.
The year-on-year increase put M2 growth within the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth for the third consecutive month.
February's M2 money supply growth was 9.88 percent year-on-year.
Economists have noted slowly increasing money demand amid a gradual economic recovery, although most of the money have flooded into a stock market that has seen dramatic rises in 1997.
The central bank said it revised its definition of M2 to reflect Taiwan's liberalising financial infrastructure.
According to the central bank's previous definition, M1A was cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits. M1B was M1A plus savings accounts. M2 was M1B plus quasi-money.

Under the revision, the central bank said it was retaining its M1A an M1B definitions, but redefining M2 as M1B plus time deposits, foreign currency deposits, postal funds, repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings.

The new M2 definition uses the post offices' total deposits instead of their redeposits in banks, adds repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings, and deletes the net value of financial bonds, savings bonds and treasury bills and foreign-currency trust funds.
